ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the right-angled triangle $ABC$, where $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $AC = 3$, and $BC = 4$, point $M$ is a point on side $AB$ (not coinciding with points $A$ or $B$). Construct $ME \perp AC$ at point $E$ and $MF \perp BC$ at point $F$. What is the minimum value of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect CM, \\
$\because$ ME $\perp$ AC, and MF $\perp$ BC, \\
$\therefore \angle$ MEC = $\angle$ MFC = 90$^\circ$, \\
$\because \angle$ C = 90$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral ECFM is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ EF = CM, \\
When CM $\perp$ AB, CM is at its shortest, as shown in the figure: \\
When CM $\perp$ AB, \\
$S_{\triangle ABC} = \frac{1}{2}AC \cdot BC = \frac{1}{2}AB \cdot CM$, \\
$\therefore \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 = \frac{1}{2}CM \cdot AB$, \\
$\because$ In Rt $\triangle$ ABC, \\
$AB = \sqrt{AC^2 + BC^2} = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$, \\
$\therefore \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 = \frac{1}{2}CM \times 5$, \\
$\therefore$ CM = 2.4, \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of CM is 2.4, \\
$\therefore$ EF = CM = 2.4, \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of EF is $\boxed{2.4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a right triangle ABC, point C is at the lower right, point A is directly above C, and point B is at the lower left; AC is the vertical side, and BC is the horizontal side, so ∠ACB is a right angle. Point M is located on the hypotenuse AB. From M, draw a vertical line downward to BC, with foot F; from M, draw a horizontal line to the right to AC, with foot E; the segment EF is also drawn in the figure. Reasoning: Connect CM. Because ME is perpendicular to AC, MF is perpendicular to BC, and AC is perpendicular to BC, all four angles of quadrilateral ECFM are right angles, so it is a rectangle. In rectangle ECFM, EF and CM are two diagonals, therefore EF = CM. Thus to find the minimum value of EF is equivalent to finding the minimum value of CM when M moves on AB. The shortest distance from a point to a line is the perpendicular segment, so when CM ⟂ AB, CM is the smallest. In right triangle ABC, AC = 3 and BC = 4, so AB = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5. Using equal areas: S_△ABC = (1/2)·AC·BC = (1/2)·AB·CM_min, so (1/2)·3·4 = (1/2)·5·CM_min, solving gives CM_min = 12/5 = 2.4. Because EF = CM, the minimum value of EF is 2.4.
